review.decision: The fixed one-arm follow-up is a defensible test of whether this R7-style weighted Gaussian-NLL recipe improves the already selected R15 sparse-plus-residual-plus-EMA predictor over its stored sparse-WMSE endpoint. No design blocker found.
checks: The primary comparator is the stored R15 sparse-WMSE score on the same accepted panel, feature pipeline, fit-row normalizer, predictor initialization, row membership, and epoch order. The new NLL endpoint is the sole additional fit; it does not use the R7 score as a matched control.

The proposed loss matches R7's bounded Gaussian objective: clip labels to [-2,2], weight by absolute clipped labels, clamp logvariance to [-4,4], and normalize by the same total weight. At zero logvariance it equals the R15 weighted-MSE scalar objective; subsequent variance gradients and shared global clipping change optimization as intended.

Restoring the frozen sparse dictionary and normalizers, verifying the archive's exact producer hash/size, checking the dictionary fingerprint, and requiring recomputed fit-only normalizers to match the stored values are appropriate provenance and parity gates. They do not constitute a second control fit.

The design explicitly limits conclusions: it tests one new NLL predictor on an adaptively exposed panel, lacks a dense-NLL arm, and therefore cannot identify sparse-by-NLL synergy, fresh-fold/public performance, or the R7 loss effect independently of all pipeline history. The secondary dense-WMSE comparison is contextual only.
prelaunch_requirements: Keep R15 feature construction causal and sequence-local, apply the original fit mask/stride only after building full histories, and use no evaluation values for fitting, normalizing, or selection.

Bind the candidate's initial model fingerprint and exact R15 feature/normalizer identities to the captured R15 receipts; compare the final canonical score against R15 stored sufficient statistics without replaying the old fit.

Treat this as one paired historical comparison with no independent training replication; report the signed delta regardless of magnitude and do not imply that a positive result establishes synergy or transfer.
